title: Match Course Instructors by Specialization Tag
prompt: This problem is modeled on online learning platform datasets such as those available on Kaggle. You have two tables: `course_completions` tracks student certifications, and `instructors` stores instructor profiles. Each instructor has a specialization array (e.g., '{"data_science", "machine_learning"}'). The `completions` table records the student ID, course title, completion date (stored as TEXT in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format), instructor name (with inconsistent casing), and a primary subject tag. For each completed course, find the instructor's email and the number of specializations they have, but ONLY include rows where the course's primary subject appears in the instructor's specialization array. Your query must handle leading/trailing whitespace in instructor names and convert the completion_date text to a proper date to extract the year. Return columns: student_id, course_title, completion_year, instructor_email, specialization_count. Order by student_id, then course_title.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE course_completions (completion_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, student_id INTEGER NOT NULL, course_title TEXT NOT NULL, completion_date TEXT NOT NULL, instructor_name TEXT NOT NULL, primary_subject TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE instructors (instructor_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, full_name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL, specializations TEXT[] NOT NULL);

composite_moves: cast completion_date from TEXT to DATE using :: operator
extract year from date using EXTRACT
normalize instructor_name with TRIM and LOWER
join completions to instructors on normalized names

hints: You'll need to clean the instructor names in the completions table before joining them to the instructors table.
Use the ANY operator to check if a value exists in a PostgreSQL array column, and use ARRAY_LENGTH to count elements in the array.
The completion_date is stored as text, so you'll need to cast it to a date type before extracting the year. Also normalize names with TRIM and LOWER before joining.
answer_key: SELECT c.student_id, c.course_title, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.completion_date::DATE) AS completion_year, i.email AS instructor_email, ARRAY_LENGTH(i.specializations, 1) AS specialization_count FROM course_completions c INNER JOIN instructors i ON LOWER(TRIM(c.instructor_name)) = LOWER(i.full_name) WHERE c.primary_subject = ANY(i.specializations) ORDER BY c.student_id, c.course_title;
